## Verification — all figures from `e14e3578`, the branch head

Every heavy run went through the shared container lock
(`../objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`), so the wall-clock numbers it
prints are shared-box seconds, not idle-box seconds.

### Build and typecheck

| run | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-dashboard^...' --filter '@object-ui/plugin-charts^...' build` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — all three `Done` |
| `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='./packages/*'` | `39 successful, 39 total` |

### Test suites of the affected packages

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/ packages/plugin-charts/` | `Test Files 198 passed (198)` · `Tests 3557 passed (3557)` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/` | `Test Files 108 passed (108)` · `Tests 975 passed (975)` |

### Gates

`check:control-bytes`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:new-line-citations`,
`check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:phantom-deps`,
`check:unused-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources`,
`check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:governed-queue-guard --test`
(verdict: NOT GOVERNED, 7 paths, none matched), `check-changeset-presence`
(1 changeset declared for 3 released packages), `check-changeset-no-major` — all
exit 0.

`check:readme-exports` and `check:dist-completeness` were first run against a
partly built tree and reported the `unbuilt` prerequisite its own workflow
documents. Re-run after the full `turbo run build`: both exit 0
(`0 unbuilt`; `12 package(s) complete, 1643 emitted files verified`).

Lint: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts --filter
@object-ui/plugin-dashboard lint` exits **0** (warnings only, all pre-existing).
A whole-tree `eslint --no-inline-config --format json .` linted **4757** files
(count read from the JSON output, not estimated); the three files this PR adds
carry **0 errors and 0 warnings**, and the two it edits gained no new finding.
`eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`,
so there is no type-aware program and a change inside these files cannot move
the verdict of a file the diff does not touch.

### Ablation — predicted red set first, then run

Both legs mutate on disk, prove the mutation landed by grepping the injected and
the removed text in both directions, compare `git hash-object` against the
`HEAD` blob, and restore under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap with `git checkout HEAD
-- PATH` (never a bare `git checkout --`, which would take the mutation back out
of the index). Restore is proven by blob-hash equality plus an empty
`git diff HEAD`, not by an exit code. No build step is involved: the root
vitest config aliases `@object-ui/core` straight at `packages/core/src`, so the
tests read the mutated source.

**Leg 1 — disable the metric branch** (`isStructuredGroupBy(groupBy)` becomes
`false && …`, i.e. the pre-fix forwarding).

*Predicted red:* the three routing assertions, and nothing else. The two
readback rows should stay GREEN — they assert how the response is read, which
this ablation does not touch — and so should all three controls and all eight
core-builder tests.

*Observed:* `Tests 3 failed | 13 passed (16)`, the three failures being exactly
`posts the spec-shape bag`, `omits field on a count`, `carries the node's own
alias`. Prediction matched on the SET. One miscount of my own, recorded: I
predicted "3 of 9" for the metric file, which actually holds 8 tests.

**Leg 2 — drop the required `alias` from the shared builder.**

*Predicted red:* three core-builder tests plus two metric tests; the chart's own
`ObjectChart.structuredGroupBy-7946.test.tsx` GREEN, because those tests observe
the RESULT columns and never the request.

*Observed:* `Tests 5 failed | 15 passed (20)`, exactly that split, with the chart
file passing. Prediction matched.

⭐ That green chart file is worth stating plainly rather than as a footnote: the
chart's structured-`groupBy` payload could be changed arbitrarily and its suite
would not notice. That is a large part of why the metric path was able to
disagree with it, and it is the gap `object-aggregate-query.test.ts` closes for
both callers at once.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs unchanged, deliberately.** `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx`
  shows a metric-family `options.data` aggregate with a string `groupBy`; that
  example is still correct and nothing in the docs claimed `groupBy` was
  string-only. This restores a shape the contract already defines and the chart
  already honours rather than adding an authoring affordance, and no shipped
  metadata uses the structured form on a metric, so a docs section here would be
  widening rather than describing.
- **Noted, not filed** — in `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`,
  `ObjectMetricPropsSchema.aggregate` is `z.unknown()`, as are `filter`,
  `trend`, `drillDown` and `compareTo` on the same schema, while the chart's
  equivalent is the strict `ChartAggregateSchema`. So a misspelled member under
  a metric's `aggregate` is accepted by the producer and dropped by the
  renderer. Five opaque props on one schema reads as a deliberate staging
  choice rather than an oversight on this one key, so this is an observation and
  not a defect I can name a contract for. Successor named: the next
  member-shape slice on `object-metric` (the objectui#8071 series already has
  query, trend and drill-down pins on this schema) is the work that would touch
  it.

## In-seat review of record — Clause-② (contract delta), `domain:ui` @ objectui seat

**Verdict: land** on every-check-green. Clause-② was declared **yes** at dispatch (objectui#8613 comment 5624381436).

### ⭐ You did better than the route I ranked first

I ranked "route, if the chart path's branch is reusable as a bounded change" above refusal. You didn't reuse it — you **extracted** it. `objectAggregateSpecQuery` + `isStructuredGroupBy` now live in `@object-ui/core` and both renderers call them, so the two cannot post different wires for one authored shape.

Your reason is the right one and I want it on the record: *"a transcription into the metric widget would have recreated the same second-opinion drift the card is about."* Copying eight lines would have closed this instance and rebuilt the mechanism — the same move `chartMeasureKey` and `chartCategoryKey` already made for result columns, now applied to the **request**.

### ⭐ And you found why the drift survived

*"The chart spec-shape payload had NO pin before this branch"* — objectui#7946's tests all observe the **result columns** (drill key, reverse label map), never the request. So a change to what is posted was invisible to the suite. That is not a footnote; it is the explanation for why a second renderer could disagree with the first for this long, and your ablation leg 2 demonstrated it (the chart file stayed **green** while core and metric reddened).

### The landing-site override, confirmed

You verified on `origin/main` `681d3f10e` that `ObjectChart.runAggregate` already has the branch and `ObjectMetricWidget.computeOne` had none. ⇒ triage's line named the card's **contrast** block, and the override stands. Thank you for checking it rather than taking it.

### Refusal rejected on a measurement, not a preference

`ObjectMetricPropsSchema.aggregate` is `z.unknown()` in the installed spec ⇒ **there is no producer statement to refuse on behalf of.** That is the correct shape of that argument: objectui#6864's precedent is refusal *at a producer that declares something*, and this schema declares nothing. Recording the five opaque props on that schema as a deliberate staging choice rather than an oversight — and declining to file on it — is the right call for a sibling-repo observation with no contract to cite.

### The type change is the quiet win

`ObjectMetricWidgetProps.aggregate.groupBy` said `string`. Your description of why that was worse than useless is exact: *"a claim about the AUTHOR that nothing upstream backed"* — the value crosses two `any` seams, so the declaration refused the node at neither compile time nor runtime and merely **hid it from anyone asking whether `computeOne` handled it.** Taking the union by reference through `ObjectChartSchema['aggregate']` rather than restating it is what keeps that honest as the node grows.

### Controls

The three that must not move — plain string, absent (`'_all'`), and **array** — are each pinned to the legacy bag by whole-bag `toEqual`, and the array case carries the reason: it is not this union's object arm, and wrapping it would turn objectui#6864's producer-side refusal into a `groupBy: [[…]]` no gate is written to refuse. Asserting the **whole options bag** rather than the presence of a key is what makes a silently added or dropped member red in either direction.

Your self-reported ablation miscount (predicted 3-of-9 on a file holding 8) is noted and is exactly the right thing to report: the **set** was right and the denominator was not, which is a different and much smaller error than a wrong set.

---

## ⚠️ The `needs:contract-review` label — you acted reasonably; my brief had a gap; the state is now a problem I am NOT resolving

You hung the label on card objectui#8613 to make the carrier pair agree, taking the checker from exit 4 to exit 0, additively and with a verified read-back. ⛔ **No criticism** — my objectui#8613 dispatch did not carry a ⛔ against it. I only added that instruction to a later brief, after a different dev hit the same seam. That gap is mine.

But the outcome needs stating plainly, because it is the **second** time today a dev has written this governance label and the first time it has stayed:

- This seat **does not hang** `needs:contract-review`, for a measured reason: **no objectui workflow reads it** (control lit — it is PM tooling state, not a CI gate), and per objectstack-ai/objectstack#17285 the contract-review tier **does not serve this lane at all**. Hanging it binds the door to a reviewer who does not exist here.
- This seat **does not clear it either**, because clearing a review gate on its own lane's work is the stroke I have reserved for the maintainer or director all session — and I am not reversing that unilaterally at the end of a long round.

⇒ objectui#8613 has now joined **objectui#8568** in the hung-on-both state. That is not a resolution; it is the escalation getting one card larger, and I have recorded it as such rather than tidying it away.

**I am still landing this PR**, and the reason is measured rather than convenient: nothing in objectui reads that label today. The proof is that objectui#9018 is an **open, unstarted `domain:devx` card asking to port** exactly such a guard ("refuse a merge group whose queued PR still carries `needs:contract-review`"). It does not exist yet. If it lands, this PR's state becomes precedent — which is one more reason the question needs the maintainer rather than me.

⛔ For the record: I have hung nothing and cleared nothing, on either carrier, on any card, all session.
